settings.description: Ordered URL-regex policies for configured filter pages: [{'pattern': ..., 'policy': 'self|landing', 'target': absolute URL}]. Landing policies require an explicit target; the first matching rule wins. Empty means unmeasured, not a finding.

Ordered URL-regex policies for paginated pages: [{'pattern': ..., 'policy': 'self|first_page|landing', 'target': absolute URL}]. Non-self policies require an explicit target; the first matching rule wins. Empty means unmeasured, not a finding.

Post-crawl finding suppressions only; never narrows URLs fetched. Ordered rules use Python regex search on a finding's target_url, optional exact check IDs, and a required reason. First matching rule wins.
Post-crawl segment rules: [{'name': ..., 'rules': [{'op': 'eq|prefix|contains|regex|in|segment', 'field': ..., 'value': ...}]}]. Rules may use page fields or another segment.

Force every cache lookup to miss (a live measurement happens) while still writing the result back to the cache. Does not disable the cache; 'cache.mode=off' does that. Rejected together with cache.mode='replay', which promises the opposite guarantee.

'off' (default: no cache), 'live' (real HTTP freshness: max-age/Expires, ETag/Last-Modified revalidation), or 'replay' (serve any cached entry regardless of age, without revalidating; a URL with no entry yet is still fetched live).

After the internal frontier closes, check each recorded external destination once — opt-in, bounded by external_checks.*, never recursive. Requires discovery.external.store and a site crawl (--url); refused on the native SQLite route and in list mode.
Keep discovered external links in the report.
Follow links marked rel=nofollow instead of skipping them.
Request discovered hyperlinks (fetch them).
Keep discovered hyperlinks in the report.
Request discovered redirect targets (fetch them).
List mode only: follow a fetched page's canonical declaration through a bounded chain, recording every inspected target without adding it to the page population.
List mode only: follow a fetched redirect past its first hop to where it actually lands, recording every hop. Depth stays 0; this is a per-URL chain walk, not link discovery.
CSS selectors excluded from the saved main-content signature.
HTML element names excluded from the saved main-content signature.
Optional CSS selector for included main-content regions.
Optional CSS root within which main content is extracted.
Bounded declarative extraction rules; no executable code or arbitrary regular expressions.
Allow bounded SQLite body retention for anonymous responses carrying Cache-Control: no-store; off by default and never permits credentialed response retention.
Hops of same-host links followed on external pages that answered; 0 checks recorded destinations only. Off-host links are never followed.
Distinct external origins the opt-in check may contact at most; redirect hops count toward it, since a redirect is a request to another origin.
Redirect hops followed per external destination before the chain is recorded unresolved; hard ceiling is 10.
HTTP attempts the external check may spend, including redirect hops and retries; 0 means no phase-specific cap. Separate from limits.max_requests.

Distinct external destinations the opt-in check may fetch at most — recorded outlinks plus same-host continuations admitted under max_depth. Destinations past the budget are recorded as skipped, not silently dropped.
Host-bound extra headers for authenticated crawling: [{'host': ..., 'headers': {name: 'env:VAR_NAME'}}].
Must be true for http.credential_headers to take effect.
Extra request headers to send with every fetch. With --set, pass a JSON object.
Explicit http:// forward proxy with host and port, or env:VARIABLE containing its URL and optional username/password. No ambient proxy variables are used by a native crawl.
Explicitly allow only the configured proxy endpoint to resolve privately; target URL private-network guards remain unchanged.
Whether the resolved proxy used authentication; managed by the crawler.
Resolved nonsecret proxy endpoint; managed by the crawler, not user input.
Number of retries after a request times out.
Per-request timeout in seconds.
Request User-Agent string; empty uses the toolkit's identifiable default.
Wall-clock budget for the whole crawl; 0 means no limit.
Maximum link depth from the start URL; -1 disables the depth limit for native SQLite site scans.
Maximum distinct query strings kept per URL path.

Total HTTP attempts for the crawl, including bootstrap, redirects and retries; 0 means no total-attempt limit. Explicit values may be at most 2,000,000, allowing robots, sitemaps, redirects and retries above the URL budget.
Response bodies larger than this are truncated before parsing.
URLs longer than this are not fetched.

Maximum number of URLs the crawl will fetch; 0 disables the URL limit for native SQLite site scans, which collect until their queue is exhausted. Values above 1,000,000 are refused rather than clamped; narrow the scope instead.
Store each link's full rel tokens, target attribute, and raw (pre-resolution) href -- needed for unsafe-cross-origin-link and protocol-relative-link detection, at a real memory cost on a large crawl.
Classify each link's DOM ancestry (nav/header/sidebar/footer/content) as it is parsed, at no extra requests; off by default because storing a position per link costs memory on a large crawl.
Ordered [{'position', 'selector'}] overrides for the built-in nav/header/sidebar/footer selectors; empty keeps the built-ins. Only read when classify is true.
Directory to write pages.jsonl and audit.json into; empty writes nothing to disk.
Write one JSON line per exclusion decision to decisions.jsonl, naming the URL and the rule that rejected it — see seohead.checks.logscan for what reads it.
Write one JSON line per fetched page to pages.jsonl.
Write the prioritized backlog beside audit.json as tasks.json and tasks.md — the same pipeline `sf run --tasks` uses, run over this crawl's own audit.
Capture browser console error messages per rendered URL.
Save a full-page screenshot per rendered URL.
Device scale factor used for rendering.

Headless engine Playwright launches: 'chromium', 'firefox' or 'webkit'. An unsupported name fails validation; an uninstalled browser binary reports a distinct install hint. Firefox cannot emulate a mobile viewport (is_mobile).
Replace same-origin iframes with their own document's body content before capture.
Merge open shadow roots into their host elements before capturing the DOM.
Emulate a mobile device (touch UA, is_mobile).
Maximum browser pages/contexts rendered at once during JS escalation; 1 keeps sequential behaviour. A rendering bound, not HTTP crawl concurrency.
Unavailable with the pinned renderer: requested persistent profiles return an explicit unavailable result and are not opened. Off by default.
Directory for the persistent profile; required when persistent_profile is true, and never a computed default.
Name of an environment variable containing the remote ws/wss endpoint; never store the endpoint in a scan.
Operator-declared remote Playwright version; its major/minor must match the installed client.
Remote browser protocol; only Playwright is supported, not CDP.
Grow the viewport to the rendered page's own height before capture, capped by resize_to_content_max_height_px.
Deterministic cap on resize_to_content, so an unbounded page is truncated rather than crawled forever.
How long JavaScript may keep running after the page and its subresources have loaded, before the DOM is captured.
Emulate touch input.
Launch a local browser (default) or connect to an explicitly supplied remote Playwright server.
Viewport preset used for rendering: 'desktop' or 'mobile'.
Custom viewport height in CSS pixels (0 = unset). Must be set together with viewport_width; the pair overrides the named preset's dimensions.
Custom viewport width in CSS pixels (0 = unset). Must be set together with viewport_height; the pair overrides the named preset's dimensions.
Page-load strategy before script_timeout_seconds starts counting down: 'load', 'domcontentloaded', or 'networkidle'.
Wall-clock budget for the escalation step; 0 means no limit.
Maximum number of pages re-fetched under the fuller representation, across all escalated patterns combined.
Sample template patterns or render every eligible URL within the independent URL/time budgets.
URLs probed raw-versus-fuller per detected template pattern before deciding whether the whole pattern needs escalation.
'raw' (static HTML only), 'legacy_fragment' (honour a page's own '_escaped_fragment_' opt-in), or 'js' (execute JavaScript in a headless browser, selectively -- see rendering.escalation).
Admit eligible rendered-link candidates through the normal bounded crawl frontier; independent of rendered route evidence storage.
Store eligible a[href] route observations from static and rendered documents; this records evidence only and never crawls discovered routes.
SQLite only: opt in to fetching directly declared same-origin scripts and stylesheets; never follows CSS imports or JavaScript modules.
scan.v2 only: total bytes accepted by the declared-resource graph.
scan.v2 only: maximum bytes accepted from one declared resource.
scan.v2 only: CSS import/url nesting depth.
scan.v2 only: maximum admitted resource origins.
scan.v2 only: maximum redirects per declared resource.
scan.v2 only: bounded deduplicated declared-resource fetch count.
scan.v2 only: resource graph wall-clock budget; 0 means no graph-specific limit.
SQLite only: maximum resource HTTP attempts, including redirects and retries; independent of the page URL limit.
SQLite only: maximum content-decoded bytes per resource response; total crawl time and body-store limits still apply.
'respect' (obey), 'report_only' (fetch, report what would be blocked, crawl anyway), or 'ignore' (do not fetch robots.txt).
Stop the crawl if robots.txt cannot be fetched at all.
The User-Agent token matched against robots.txt rules.
Filename suffix denylist for discovered routes; matches the final URL-path suffix, without query or fragment. Exclusions take precedence over the extension allowlist.
Hosts never fetched regardless of what links to them.
Response Content-Type denylist checked after fetch and before parsing or body retention; supports exact types and type wildcards such as image/*. Exclusions take precedence.
Regexes; a discovered link matching any of these is not followed.

Optional filename suffix allowlist for discovered routes (for example ['html', 'pdf']); matches the final URL-path suffix, without query or fragment. If set, extensionless routes are not included. Exclusions take precedence.

Optional response Content-Type allowlist checked after fetch and before parsing or body retention; supports exact types and type wildcards such as image/*. A missing or malformed type is recorded as unavailable when this list is set.
Regexes; a discovered link must match at least one to be followed.

Which discovered URLs count as internal: 'host' (conservative) or 'registrable_domain' (also accepts subdomains -- on a shared hosting suffix such as github.io or vercel.app, only the audited tenant's own subdomain, never another tenant's, per seohead.recon.net.registrable_domain).

Ordered, first-match-wins named segments for a multilingual or multi-regional site: [{'name': ..., 'prefix': '/en/', 'host': 'en.example.com', 'pattern': '...'}, ...] -- at least one of prefix/host/pattern per entry. A URL matching none of them is the built-in 'default' segment, so every URL belongs to exactly one segment, always.
Fetch only these segment names (plus 'default' when named); empty means every segment is in scope. Subsumes a subfolder-only or single-subdomain crawl without an ad-hoc scope.include_patterns regex.
Seed the crawl from the sitemap declared in robots.txt when no explicit sitemap URL is given.
Increase the delay automatically when the target slows down or times out.
Per-origin ceiling on requests in flight at once. The adaptive throttle starts well below it and only grows toward it on sustained success; 1 is sequential.
Maximum delay adaptive back-off may reach.
Minimum delay between requests; the floor beneath adaptive back-off.
Stop the crawl after this many timeouts in a row.
SQLite only: captured_entity_bytes retains fetched HTML/DOM; off retains metadata only.

'stable' (default) admits explicit URL limits up to 1,000,000; native SQLite max_urls=0 disables the URL limit while retaining independent resource guards. 'experimental_synthetic' is the compatible direct-storage fixture marker; live collectors refuse that marker. Neither setting certifies measured capacity.
Explicit scan storage format: scan.v1 (default) or scan.v2 for optional graph/event extensions.
SQLite only: history-size warning threshold; never enables automatic deletion.
SQLite only: maximum decoded bytes retained for one complete body.
SQLite only: total unique encoded body bytes retained per scan.
SQLite only: filesystem reserve; low space interrupts collection with a checkpoint.
